sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Semantic conventions

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Collector distributions

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: OTLP receiver component

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Batch processor component
sources.supportRationale: Batch processing has component-specific stability; batching is not durable backend storage.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Transform processor component
sources.supportRationale: Transform support/status and error behavior are component-specific.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Collector configuration
sources.supportRationale: Collector components must be configured and enabled in the service pipeline.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Collector resiliency
sources.supportRationale: Queue, retry, persistence and exporter behavior bound telemetry loss during outages.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Collector
sources.supportRationale: Collector receive/process/export responsibilities and component stability differ from backend storage and visualization.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Context propagation
sources.supportRationale: Trace context relates activity across asynchronous and network boundaries without being an authorization credential.

scenarios.theme: An auto agent creates the same HTTP spans as manual middleware. What will you keep?
scenarios.assumptions: The trace tree duplicates request operations and a request counter appears doubled after rollout. What diagnosis fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An auto agent creates the same HTTP spans as manual middleware. What will you keep?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Inventory instrumentation paths and SDK/provider setup, choose one owner per standard boundary and retain manual business spans where they add distinct mea

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Removing every manual span can lose business context; keeping overlapping counters makes aggregate rates wrong

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Similar names alone do not prove duplication, so inspect actual source/scope and events.

scenarios.theme: The backend is unavailable for five minutes. Can a 30-second queue preserve everything?
scenarios.assumptions: Input is 10,000 spans/s and a hypothetical span-counted queue holds 300,000 with no successful export. What capacity/policy fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The backend is unavailable for five minutes. Can a 30-second queue preserve everything?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Calculate the 30-second raw coverage under those assumptions, then choose an explicit retention/loss budget, bounded storage/retry policy and recovery thro

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A real queue may count requests/bytes instead of spans; persistent storage survives only defined failures

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Larger queues cost memory/disk and do not guarantee exactly-once delivery or infinite outages.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to resiliency, collector; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: Each customer gets a different service.name and dashboards fragment. What identity belongs where?
scenarios.assumptions: A team uses customer IDs as service identity and sends raw personal fields as attributes. What redesign fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Each customer gets a different service.name and dashboards fragment. What identity belongs where?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use stable bounded service/resource identity, select appropriate bounded measurement attributes and minimize/redact personal data before export

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Simply hashing customer values preserves high cardinality and may preserve privacy risk

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A central transform helps enforce policy but does not remove already persisted copies or replace source minimization.
